symptom: Fatal error 'Unsupported Prime raw color texture-copy mode' when opening the scan visor
diagnosis: PE pixel format 3 (Z24) marks a depth copy (GXCopyTex switches the PE format for Z destinations). The 4-bit copy format 0xB is GX_TF_Z16, which the SDK encodes as 11 (libogc GX_SetTexCopyDst: if fmt == GX_TF_Z16 lfmt = 11). Rectangle 32x32 at (278,126); stride 256 bytes = 8 Z16 blocks of 32 bytes. The raw-BP adapter only accepted colour copies.
fix: runtime/include/hle/prime_raw_bp.h DecodeColorCopy: depth sources map nibble 1 -> GX_TF_Z8 (8x4 blocks), 0xB -> GX_TF_Z16 (4x4, 16 bpp), 6 -> GX_TF_Z24X8 (4x4, 32 bpp), the depth formats Aurora resolves from the depth buffer; other depth nibbles (Z4, Z8M, Z8L, Z16L) still reject explicitly.
tests: gx_fifo_storage_tests: scan-visor Z16 copy decodes to format 0x13, 32x32, 2048 bytes; Z8 decodes; Z8M rejects; existing colour cases unchanged. Both input/FIFO test executables pass.
follow_ups: Second visor copy: GX_CTF_Z8L (nibble 0xA). Added Z4/Z8M/Z8L/Z16L depth conversions (upstream aurora semantics) and their sample-format compatibility; see 20261024_upstream_aurora_selected.json.

The visor then reads the Z8L copy on the CPU: 'Unsupported CPU-visible EFB copy format 0x3a'. efb_ram_encoder.cpp now describes GX_CTF_Z4 as I4, GX_TF_Z8/GX_CTF_Z8M/GX_CTF_Z8L as I8 and GX_CTF_Z16L as IA8 (the conversion leaves the depth byte in R and the second byte in A, so IA8 Z16 lands as [middle, high]).
follow_up_intensity: Third visor copy rejected: trigger=0x18213 pe=0x41 source 640x448 half-scale, stride 1280. BP bit 15 selects the intensity copy formats (nibble 1 = GX_TF_I8 -> 320x224). prime_raw_bp.h now accepts GX_TF_I4/I8/IA4/IA8 (nibbles 0-3) with their block shapes (I4 8x8, I8/IA4 8x4, IA8 4x4); Aurora already converts and RAM-encodes them. Test added for the exact visor registers.

scan_targeting.symptom: Visor opens but nothing can be scanned and the blue outline of scannable objects is missing
scan_targeting.capture: capture_20261024_022256: scene draws tag objects with dst alpha IDs (12, 24, 32, 40, 52, 68, 80; 0 = not scannable, blend ONE/ZERO so the shader dst-alpha path writes them). Then A8 91x62 (host) around the reticle, Z16 and Z8L of the same rectangle, a full-screen A8 and the half-scale I8.
scan_targeting.cause: The game reads the reticle probe copies on the CPU. Aurora downloaded CPU-visible copies only up to 256 bytes (lens-flare probe); the visor's A8 (~768 bytes), Z16 (2048) and Z8L (1024) stayed GPU-only, so guest RAM was stale and no target was found.
scan_targeting.fix: aurora lib/gfx/efb_ram_copy.cpp: kAsyncReadbackMaxBytes 256 -> 4096 (asynchronous, one-frame-late readback, 32 destination slots).

scan_visuals.symptom: Scanning works, but the blue outline/tint of scannable objects is missing (Wii reference: trooper rimmed and tinted blue, scene dimmed)
scan_visuals.capture: capture_20261024_024110 with WII_COMPILED_DRAW_DUMP_ALL_COPIES: copy3 saves the top-left quarter (0x8073c3c0); copy4 = full-screen A8 object IDs (0x90118800, correct: trooper 80, others 8/32/60...); copy5 = half-scale I8 scene; draw 442 (9 TEV stages) samples the ID copy as I8 (neighbour-equality edge count) and as C8 (palette colour per ID) into the quarter; copy6 = result (0x90118800); draw 443 restores the quarter, draw 444 composites the result full screen.
scan_visuals.finding: copy6 had the dimmed grey scene but every tagged object black/alpha 0: the C8 lookup returned nothing. copy_ref_matches_texobj required copy_texture_format_compatible(A8, C8), which was false, so the C8 sample read guest RAM (never downloaded for a full-screen copy) instead of the dynamic palette conversion of the copy.
scan_visuals.fix: aurora gx.hpp copy_texture_format_compatible: 8-bit copies (A8, R8, G8, B8, I8, Z8, Z8M, Z8L) are sampleable as GX_TF_C8 and 4-bit copies (R4, I4, Z4) as GX_TF_C4, through resolve_dynamic_palette_texture (index from the copy texture's R channel). C14X2 stays unmatched.

validation.user: scan visor colours and outlines now match the Wii reference (trooper, crates, tank, door); top-left artefact gone
